title: Getting around
goal: Ask for and understand directions, take buses and taxis, and tell people what to do (politely or casually).
intro:
Nepali towns rarely use street addresses: people navigate by **चोक** (squares/junctions), temples, shops and landmarks, and they ask a lot. This unit gives you the words for directions and transport, and the grammar to tell a taxi driver where to go.

The main grammar point is the **imperative** — the command form — which, like everything else in Nepali, changes with the level of respect: बस (to a friend), बस्नुहोस् (polite).

vocab.note: Many neighbourhoods are named after them: न्यू रोड चोक, ठमेल चोक.
A suspension bridge in the hills is झोलुङ्गे पुल.
Long-distance tourist buses, city buses (सिटी बस).

vocab.en: to reach, arrive; to be enough

vocab.note: यहीँ रोक्नुहोस् 'stop right here'. To stop (oneself): रोकिनु.

vocab.en: to get on, board; to climb
to get off; to go down
towards, in the direction of; around
up to, as far as, until

phrases.en: Excuse me, which way is the bus station?
How long does it take on foot?
Will you go to Boudha? (to a taxi driver)
Please take me to this place.
Could you show me on the map?

grammar.title: The imperative at four levels
grammar.body:
The command form follows the honorific system:

**तँ** — bare stem: गर्, बस्, खा, जा (and irregular आइज 'come!')
**तिमी** — stem + **-अ**: गर, बस, पढ; vowel stems take **-ऊ**: खाऊ, जाऊ, आऊ, देऊ (give)
**तपाईं** — **-नुहोस्**: गर्नुहोस्, बस्नुहोस्, जानुहोस्, आउनुहोस्. In quick speech this shrinks to **-नुस्**: बस्नुस्, आउनुस्.
**Royal / highest honorific** — **-इबक्सियोस्**: गरिबक्सियोस्. You'll mainly see this in very formal invitations; to हजुर in everyday speech you simply use the -नुहोस् forms.

**Negative**: add **न-** in front: **नगर** 'don't do' (तिमी), **नजानुहोस्** 'please don't go', **नरोक्नुहोस्** 'don't stop'.

Soften commands with **न** after them (बस्नुहोस् न 'do sit down') or **त** (हेर्नुहोस् त 'just have a look').

grammar.title: Going places: -मा, -तिर, -बाट, -सम्म
grammar.body:
With **जानु** 'go' and **आउनु** 'come', the destination often needs **no ending at all**: म बजार जान्छु 'I'm going to the market', घर आऊ 'come home'. You can also use **-मा**: पोखरामा जान्छु.

• **-तिर** 'towards, -wards': बजारतिर 'towards the market', माथितिर 'upwards'. Also 'around (time)': सात बजेतिर.
• **-बाट** 'from; via; by means of': घरबाट 'from home', पुलबाट 'over the bridge', बसबाट 'by bus'.
• **-सम्म** 'as far as, up to': चोकसम्म 'as far as the junction'.
• **-देखि … -सम्म** 'from … to': काठमाडौंदेखि पोखरासम्म.
• **-मा** with vehicles: बसमा 'on the bus', ट्याक्सीमा 'in a taxi'.

To describe a place's location, Nepali often uses **पर्नु** 'to fall/lie': बैंक बायाँ पर्छ 'the bank is on the left'.

examples.en: I'm on my way to the office.
We came from Kathmandu by bus.
Go straight as far as the bridge.
The temple is on the right side of the road.

dialogue.title: Taxi to Boudha
dialogue.setting: Tom flags down a taxi in Thamel to go to the great stupa at Boudha (Boudhanath).

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.native: धेरै भयो, दाइ। पाँच सयमा जाऊँ न।
lines.roman: dherai bhayo, dāi. pāṃch sayamā jāuṃ na.
lines.en: That's too much. Let's go for five hundred.

lines.speaker: Driver
lines.native: ट्राफिक धेरै छ। सात सय दिनुहोस्।
lines.roman: ṭrāphik dherai chha. sāt saya dinuhos.
lines.en: There's a lot of traffic. Give me seven hundred.

lines.speaker: Driver
lines.en: We're at Boudha. Which way now?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.native: सिधा जानुहोस्, अनि गेटको अगाडि बायाँ मोडिनुहोस्। … यहीँ रोक्नुहोस्।
lines.roman: sidhā jānuhos, ani geṭko agāḍi bāyāṃ moḍinuhos. … yahiṃ roknuhos.
lines.en: Go straight, then turn left in front of the gate. … Stop right here.

culture: Directions in Nepal are given by **landmarks**, not street names: 'past the chok, near the temple, opposite the bank'. If you ask three people you may get three answers — ask again near your destination. Taxis officially have meters but fares are usually agreed in advance; ride apps are popular in Kathmandu. Microbuses and buses have a conductor (खलासी/कन्डक्टर) who shouts the route and collects fares — say **ओर्लने!** or **रोक्नुस्!** when you want to get off. On trekking trails you'll learn the joke **'नेपाली फ्ल्याट'**: 'Nepali flat' means a little bit up, a little bit down — all day long.

tip.title: कता पर्छ? — which way is it?
tip.body:
- To ask where a place is, Nepalis say **कता पर्छ?** 'which way does it lie?' (from पर्नु 'to fall, lie').
- Answer with **यता** 'this way', **उता** 'that way', or a landmark + **पर्छ**: बैंक मन्दिरको छेउमा पर्छ.
- Stop a stranger with **माफ गर्नुहोस्** 'excuse me'.
tip.pattern: place + कता पर्छ?  →  यता / उता पर्छ

sentences.en: Excuse me, which way is the bank?
The temple is this way.

sentences.native: बसपार्क उता पर्छ, धेरै टाढा छैन।
sentences.roman: baspārk utā parchha, dherai ṭāḍhā chhaina.
sentences.en: The bus station is that way, it's not very far.
The bank is beside the temple.
Which way is this place? (showing an address)
Is that place far from here?
No, it's close by.
Is this the way to the bus station?
I don't know the way.

tip.title: Telling someone what to do
tip.body:
- Polite (तपाईं): stem + **-नुहोस्**: जा**नुहोस्** 'please go', मोडि**नुहोस्** 'please turn'. In quick speech it shrinks to **-नुस्**.
- Friendly (तिमी): stem + **-अ** (पर्ख, बस) or **-ऊ** after a vowel (जाऊ, आऊ).
- 'Don't': put **न-** in front: **न**जानुहोस्, **न**जाऊ.
tip.pattern: जा + नुहोस् → जानुहोस्  ·  तिमी: जाऊ  ·  नजानुहोस्

sentences.en: Go straight on. (polite)
Turn right at the junction. (polite)
Turn left at the next bend. (polite)
Don't go over the bridge, the road isn't good. (polite)
Please show me the way.
Wait for me at the junction. (polite)

sentences.native: तिमी चोकमा पर्ख, म आउँदै छु।
sentences.roman: timi chokmā parkha, ma āuṃdai chhu.
sentences.en: Wait at the junction, I'm on my way. (to a friend)
Don't go that way, come this way. (to a friend)
The temple is next to the bridge.
Not left, right!

tip.title: From, towards, as far as
tip.body:
- **-मा** with vehicles: बस**मा** 'on the bus'.
- **-बाट** 'from': घर**बाट** 'from home'. **-तिर** 'towards': ठमेल**तिर**. **-सम्म** 'as far as': पोखरा**सम्म**.
- With जानु the destination needs no ending: म ठमेल जान्छु 'I'm going to Thamel'.

sentences.en: Does this bus go all the way to Pokhara?
I'll go by bus.
Get on the microbus, it goes towards Thamel.
Take the Pokhara bus from the bus station.
I'll get off at the junction.
This microbus goes as far as the bus station.
Which bus goes towards the temple?
I go from home to the office by bus.

sentences.native: बस धेरै ढिलो छ, म हिँडेर जान्छु।
sentences.roman: bas dherai ḍhilo chha, ma hiṃḍera jānchhu.
sentences.en: The bus is very slow, I'll walk.
I'll get off in front of the bank. (to the conductor)

tip.title: Talking to drivers
tip.body:
- Call a driver or conductor **दाइ** 'big brother' (**भाइ** if he's clearly younger).
- Ask 'will you go to…?' with the polite verb: बौद्ध **जानुहुन्छ**?
- Soften a request with **न** after it: बिस्तारै जानुहोस् **न** 'do go slowly'.
- Agree the fare before you get in.

sentences.en: Will you go to the airport? (to a taxi driver)
Please take me to the bus station.
How much is the fare to the airport?
That fare's too much.
Stop in front of the bank, please.
Don't stop here, stop a bit further on.
Please go slowly.
Could you open the window, please?
I need a taxi.
We'll be there in ten minutes.
Is your taxi free?

tip.title: कति समय लाग्छ? — how long?
tip.body:
- **लाग्नु** also means 'to take' (time or money): कति समय **लाग्छ**? 'how long does it take?'
- Answer with the time + **लाग्छ**: दस मिनेट लाग्छ. Add **जति** for 'about'.
- 'It doesn't take long': धेरै समय **लाग्दैन**.
- **हिँडेर** = on foot, **ट्याक्सीमा** = by taxi.

sentences.en: How long does it take to the bus station?
It takes half an hour on foot.
About five minutes by taxi.

sentences.native: उकालो छ, एक घण्टा जति लाग्छ।
sentences.roman: ukālo chha, ek ghanṭā jati lāgchha.
sentences.en: It's uphill, it takes about an hour.
How long does it take to the airport by taxi?
It doesn't take long.
Now it's downhill, it's easy.
Where is the temple on the map?
I don't have a map.
